name: Bitcoin
day_summary: BTC gave back ~1% on FOMC Day 1, trading from a $66,923 early-session high down to a $65,350 intraday low as of the mid-morning session (~10:40 AM ET). Price is currently hovering at $65,633 — comfortably above the $65,000 re-risk trigger but consolidating below the $66,831 session high from June 15. The day's most important event is not BTC-specific: BlackRock launched BITA (the iShares Bitcoin Premium Income ETF) on Nasdaq today — the first yield Bitcoin ETF in history, targeting 15–25% annual income via covered-call overlays on IBIT. This is a new institutional demand vector layering onto the existing spot ETF bid. Bears won the session on price, but the structural bid is visibly expanding. FOMC opens today; Warsh's press conference June 17 is the week's binary.

analysis:
## FOMC Day 1 — consolidating above the trigger

BTC is giving back ~1% on FOMC Day 1, trading at **$65,633** with a session range of $65,350–$66,923. That range tells the story cleanly: bulls tested the $67K level again in early Asia/London trading and got turned back; bears pressed the $65,350 low and couldn't push through. The $65,000 re-risk trigger from the June 15 BUY call is holding as support. This is FOMC-wait mode, not a regime change.

## BlackRock BITA: a new institutional demand category

[BlackRock launched BITA on Nasdaq today](https://news.bitcoin.com/blackrock-beats-goldman-to-market-with-bitcoin-income-etf-bita-launching-june-16/) — the first yield-generating Bitcoin ETF in history, targeting 15–25% annual income via a covered-call overlay on IBIT. This is structurally significant beyond the headline: income-generating BTC wrappers attract insurance companies, pension funds, and income mandates that are blocked from holding raw spot BTC by their investment policy statements. BITA doesn't just add to AUM; it unlocks a new demand pool. [Goldman Sachs is reportedly racing to bring a competing product to market](https://coingape.com/nasdaq-confirms-blackrock-bitcoin-premium-income-etf-listing-on-june-16/) — the competitive signal confirms this is a viable market segment, not a one-off experiment.

## The structural BUY thesis remains intact

The macro mechanism that drove the June 15 BUY call is end-to-end intact: Hormuz reopening → oil lower (~$80 Brent) → inflation expectations fall → dollar retreats (DXY ~97.80, well below 100) → BTC discount rate falls. Spot ETF inflows confirmed at $85.8M net on June 13 — the institutional bid is back. [BTC is above $65K, above the $66K re-entry threshold, and above every key moving average](https://blockchainreporter.net/bitcoin-price-today-btc-holds-66k-as-the-feds-big-day-arrives-and-warsh-takes-over/). The regime is intact.

## Why HOLD not BUY today

The call shifts from BUY to **HOLD** for one session: FOMC Day 1 is the worst moment to add size into a crowded long book. Put/call at 0.90, funding still positive, momentum longs pressed — the flush risk on a Warsh hawkish surprise is the most violent of the cycle. A non-hawkish Fed tomorrow clears the last gate and the crowd chases $70K. Keep dry powder, stop on existing position at $63,500 daily close, and let Wednesday resolve.
